entries.title: Job 7:1
segments: ¶Has not man his ordered time of trouble on the earth? and are not his days like the days of a servant working for payment?

entries.title: Job 7:2
segments: As a servant desiring the shades of evening, and a workman looking for his payment:

entries.title: Job 7:3
segments: So I have for my heritage months of pain to no purpose, and nights of weariness are given to me.

entries.title: Job 7:4
segments: When I go to my bed, I say, When will it be time to get up? but the night is long, and I am turning from side to side till morning light.

entries.title: Job 7:5
segments: My flesh is covered with worms and dust; my skin gets hard and then is cracked again.

entries.title: Job 7:6
segments: My days go quicker than the cloth-worker's thread, and come to an end without hope.

entries.title: Job 7:7
segments: ¶O, keep in mind that my life is wind: my eye will never again see good.

entries.title: Job 7:8
segments: The eye of him who sees me will see me no longer: your eyes will be looking for me, but I will be gone.

entries.title: Job 7:9
segments: A cloud comes to an end and is gone; so he who goes down into the underworld comes not up again.

entries.title: Job 7:10
segments: He will not come back to his house, and his place will have no more knowledge of him.

entries.title: Job 7:11
segments: So I will not keep my mouth shut; I will let the words come from it in the pain of my spirit, my soul will make a bitter outcry.

entries.title: Job 7:12
segments: Am I a sea, or a sea-beast, that you put a watch over me?

entries.title: Job 7:13
segments: When I say, In my bed I will have comfort, there I will get rest from my disease;

entries.title: Job 7:14
segments: Then you send dreams to me, and visions of fear;

entries.title: Job 7:15
segments: So that a hard death seems better to my soul than my pains.

entries.title: Job 7:16
segments: I have no desire for life, I would not be living for ever! Keep away from me, for my days are as a breath.

entries.title: Job 7:17
segments: ¶What is man, that you have made him great, and that your attention is fixed on him,

entries.title: Job 7:18
segments: And that your hand is on him every morning, and that you are testing him every minute?

entries.title: Job 7:19
segments: How long will it be before your eyes are turned away from me, so that I may have a minute's breathing-space?

entries.title: Job 7:20
segments: If I have done wrong, what have I done to you, O keeper of men? why have you made me a mark for your blows, so that I am a weariness to myself?

entries.title: Job 7:21
segments: And why do you not take away my sin, and let my wrongdoing be ended? for now I go down to the dust, and you will be searching for me with care, but I will be gone.
